short: The radical remnant of the Long Parliament that oversaw the execution of King Charles I and the establishment of the English Republic.
full:
Following Pride's Purge in December 1648, the "Rump" was the small faction of the Long Parliament that remained to govern England. Comprising less than a third of the original House of Commons, it was entirely dependent on the military power of the New Model Army. In January 1649, this body took the monumental steps of passing an act to try King Charles I for high treason, abolishing the monarchy, and declaring England a Commonwealth.

For the next four years, the Rump Parliament struggled to balance the radical demands of the army with the necessity of establishing a stable, legitimate government. It successfully oversaw the brutal military subjugation of Ireland and Scotland, expanding the Commonwealth's borders. However, its failure to agree on new elections or substantial domestic reforms eventually frustrated Oliver Cromwell, who forcibly dissolved the Rump in April 1653.
